identity.description: Unpenalized least squares fit with the FULL inference apparatus: coefficients with standard errors, t-statistics, p-values, confidence intervals, and prediction intervals. This is the family's answer-the-why member — where sklearn's linear models predict, OLS testifies. Requires n > p and honest attention to its error assumptions.

emits.note: get_prediction() yields mean CIs AND per-row prediction intervals under the Gaussian-error assumption
the genuine coefficients+SE emission: params/bse/pvalues/conf_int — the inference story the sklearn siblings cannot tell

cov_type.note: an INFERENCE choice, never CV-searched: HC3 when heteroscedasticity is detected, HAC for serial correlation

method.note: fit() solve method; qr is the numerically safer choice on ill-conditioned X

missing.note: 'drop' silently listwise-deletes — biased unless MCAR; the pipeline should impute upstream instead

hyperparameters.note: OLS has NO regularization knob — nothing here is searchable; the model is fully determined by the data. That absence IS the inference guarantee (unbiasedness under Gauss-Markov).

invariances.why: coefficients and SEs are per-unit quantities — magnitudes are incomparable across unscaled features and kappa(X'X) conditioning degrades; NOTE the fit itself is scale-EQUIVARIANT (predictions and p-values unchanged under rescaling), so scaling is comparability + numerics, not identification
the conditional mean is assumed linear in the supplied columns; log/rank of a covariate is a different model
the normal equations have no missingness model; missing='drop' merely listwise-deletes, which biases the sample unless MCAR
the array API needs a pre-encoded design matrix (formula API delegates encoding to patsy, outside this driver)
the whole inference product rests on Gauss-Markov + Gaussian errors: linear mean, homoscedastic, independent errors — violate them and the SEs/p-values (the reason to choose OLS) are wrong
exact small-sample t/F inference is OLS's home turf — but it strictly requires n > p for positive residual degrees of freedom
the linear predictor extends beyond the training range; prediction intervals widen with leverage but the mean keeps moving linearly

featureStats.why: VIF_j = 1/(1-R2_j) is EXACTLY the multiplier on coefficient variance — the direct diagnosis of why a CI is wide when features are collinear
large kappa(X) means the X'X inversion amplifies noise into the coefficients; statsmodels prints this in summary() and warns on it
Breusch-Pagan rejecting homoscedasticity invalidates nonrobust SEs — the mechanical trigger for cov_type='HC3'
exact t/F inference leans on Gaussian errors in small samples; a failed Jarque-Bera downgrades CIs to asymptotic-only

modelMetrics.why: in-sample fit penalized for parameter count — the honest OLS scoreboard, since raw R2 can only rise as p grows
under squared loss a single influential row can move the whole coefficient vector; Cook's D localizes exactly which row is doing it

edgeCases.behavior: the default pinv solve SILENTLY returns the minimum-norm solution; SEs on the involved columns are meaningless
edgeCases.note: condition-number check; drop or combine the collinear columns

edgeCases.behavior: zero (or negative) residual degrees of freedom — SEs/p-values undefined
edgeCases.note: bank-entry route: ridge/lasso for prediction-only on wide data

edgeCases.behavior: coefficients stay unbiased but nonrobust SEs (and every p-value built on them) are wrong
statsmodels does NOT auto-add a constant — the regression is forced through the origin and R2 is redefined
edgeCases.note: the wrapper must add_constant; this is the classic statsmodels trap

edgeCases.behavior: quadratic loss lets one row steer the fit and shrink apparent SEs

driver.wrapperNeeds: adapter: add_constant on the design matrix; sklearn-style fit(X,y)/predict facade over the results object; expose params/bse/pvalues/conf_int as the coefficients payload and get_prediction() intervals on the score port
driver.threadSafety: closed-form pinv/QR solve; the fitted results object is read-only thread-safe

placementClaims.why: no missingness model — NaN either raises or is listwise-deleted, and deletion biases the estimand unless MCAR
transforming skewed covariates/target toward linearity + normal residuals is what makes the Gaussian inference assumptions actually hold
the fit is scale-equivariant (predictions and p-values are unchanged), so scaling is not mechanically required — it buys comparable coefficient magnitudes and better X'X conditioning
categoricals must be design-encoded (with one reference level dropped, or the dummy trap creates exact collinearity)
